timestamp_caution: Contact labels identify nominal half-second sampling bins; ffmpeg fps sampling does not establish exact transition boundaries.
observed_order: Idle gray-brown flat build marker with white central build pictogram, log/material icon and reference-video cost.
Player approaches; logs transfer toward marker, marker shows green fill/green corner arcs while payment occurs.
Marker disappears; a small furnace/hearth appears.
Camp ground expands/clears around furnace, then palisade, resource storage mats and counter are present.
interpretation: The green filled marker is an active material-spend/build interaction. The finished state is replacement/removal of the marker plus result context, not a permanent full green storage tile.
limits: No canonical Havenline price, dwell timing, capacity, conversion recipe or runtime integration inferred.
Sequence supports a visible reference design state progression; exact build dependencies and all possible state transitions remain outside these sampled frames.
review_implication: For build-state concepts, preserve distinct idle, payment-in-progress and completed-marker-removed meanings. Persistent completed green pads require explicit proposal labeling.

additional_sampled_sequences.observed: Cash is collected from a black storage mat, carried to a separate brown upgrade marker; green payment is followed by construction glow and replacement of fishing rods with intake machinery. The work-area segmented outline is a distinct footprint.

An expansion action changes camp/counter context; later the axe-plus marker shows green payment and completion glow, then remains/returns with a different displayed reference price. One-time marker removal cannot be generalized to repeatable upgrades.

differentiated_completion_rule: One-time build/unlock markers can be removed/replaced by result context; repeatable upgrade markers can remain/return. State concepts must preserve this distinction and not imply every completed marker persists green or disappears.
